questions.question_text: A new e-commerce application is being developed with a focus on quality and reliability. The development team wants to ensure that the application is thoroughly tested and that any external dependencies are continuously monitored. Which two strategies should the team implement to meet these goals? (Select TWO)
options: A. Implement test-driven development and code reviews to improve code quality and minimize defects before deployment.
B. Use Amazon S3 for storing application logs and metrics to ensure data durability.
C. Deploy the application in a shared development environment to allow multiple developers to work on the same codebase simultaneously.
D. Integrate AWS X-Ray to trace requests and identify bottlenecks or failures in external services.
E. Use Amazon DevOps Guru to identify operational issues and recommend specific actions to prevent them.
questions.explanation:
A. Implement test-driven development and code reviews to improve code quality and minimize defects before deployment. This aligns with the AWS Well-Architected Framework's best practice of establishing code quality practices to minimize defects before they are deployed. By adopting practices like test-driven development and code reviews, the team can ensure that the application is thoroughly tested before it goes into production, which reduces the risk of defects and improves overall application quality. (Source: AWS Well-Architected Framework, p.166)

B. Use Amazon S3 for storing application logs and metrics to ensure data durability. While Amazon S3 is a robust storage solution, it is not directly related to the goal of improving code quality or monitoring external dependencies. It is more about data storage and not part of the development or deployment process. (Source: AWS Well-Architected Framework, p.166)

C. Deploy the application in a shared development environment to allow multiple developers to work on the same codebase simultaneously. This anti-pattern can lead to issues such as code overwriting and can hinder the development process. It is not recommended as it can introduce errors and conflicts. (Source: AWS Well-Architected Framework, p.169)

D. Integrate AWS X-Ray to trace requests and identify bottlenecks or failures in external services. AWS X-Ray is specifically designed to provide insights into application performance and the performance of external dependencies. By integrating it, the team can identify and resolve issues in real-time, ensuring the application performs optimally. (Source: AWS Well-Architected Framework, p.145)

E. Use Amazon DevOps Guru to identify operational issues and recommend specific actions to prevent them. While Amazon DevOps Guru is a valuable tool for identifying operational issues, it is more focused on operational issues rather than code quality or external dependency monitoring. It is a good practice but not the primary focus for the given scenario. (Source: AWS Well-Architected Framework, p.166)
